notes.summary: Independently proved direction-error counterexample for frozen ch51 LF2013–2059; the larger-exponent correction is valid only with decrease, eventual inclusions, and strong openness. Original DPS normalization and final-type limitations were inspected, not granted.
notes.detailedSummary: In the exp(−u) convention, I(λ log|z|²)=(z^floor λ), including integer endpoints. At λ=1 a constant log-pole sequence makes the printed λ′<λ union equal O instead of (z). The P¹ Green function supplies the same counterexample under the analytic/gentle/vanishing-loss hypotheses. Under u_j↓u, eventual I(λ′u_j)⊂I(λu) for λ′>λ, and the published strong openness theorem, the corrected λ′>λ formula follows at stalks. DPS is arXiv math/0006205v2 of 10 October 2000; φ=u/2 and its source current equals π times the book current. Whole required text units through literal LF775 were read. The final equisingular theorem does not itself supply finite logarithmic ideal norms; no publisher identity or full-PDF visual reading is asserted.
notes.text:
The following is a mathematical counterexample, not a conclusion from source histories. Fix dd^c=(i/2π)∂∂̄ and multiplier ideals defined by |f|²exp(−λu). On a disk take u_j=u=log|z|². A nonzero germ of order k is integrable precisely when 2π∫₀ᵗr^(2k−2λ+1)dr is finite, i.e. k>λ−1, equivalently k≥floor λ. Thus I(λu)=(z^floor λ), including the integer thresholds. At λ=1 the left ideal is (z); for every 0<λ′<1 each ideal I(λ′u_j) is O. Hence the printed union over λ′<λ in frozen ch51 LF2013–2059 is false.

This meets the relevant approximation conditions globally: on P¹, G=log|z|²−log(1+|z|²) satisfies ω+dd^cG=δ₀, sup G=0. The constant sequence G has zero curvature loss, decreases to G, has analytic ideal type (1/m,(z^m)) at 0, and for λ′>λ has I(λ′G)⊂I(λG). Therefore the counterexample is not excluded by gentle type or eventual inclusion hypotheses.

A separate correct assertion is: if u_j↓u, for every λ′>λ one has I(λ′u_j)⊂I(λu) for all sufficiently large j, and strong openness holds, then I(λu)=⋃_{λ′>λ}⋂_j I(λ′u_j), stalkwise. For right-to-left membership one sufficiently late inclusion suffices. For left-to-right, strong openness places f in I(λ′u) for some λ′>λ, and u≤u_j places it in every I(λ′u_j), on the same local integrability ball. Strong openness is the explicitly declared published Guan–Zhou input, not proved here; the correction is conditional on exactly those stated premises. It authenticates neither every other conclusion of the frozen proposition nor its surrounding prose. In particular, a constant zero sequence cannot decrease pointwise to a nonzero Cantor potential under the preceding printed definition.

The full frozen proposition/proof is preserved unchanged in LOCALONLY/ch51-qes-preserves-i-original-body.tex. Both frozen chapter hashes remain matched in source-inventory.json. Long source bodies remain local. The main realization proof uses capped integrals instead of either union formula.

The only private primaries used are the original bound DPS PDF/text, arXiv math/0006205v2, 10 October 2000. PDF SHA256 50709e54ee90dc7d43a9f6b583137a525bdf2195563e0b30535de970545dfa9a; text SHA256 331e3c4d85cc17e22b8b357c1c5ff6ee1fc68a02026094f995285491dd0adf46. Every literal newline record LF404–775 was physically read in bounded chunks, covering whole 2.2.1/2.2.2, Steps 1–4, and 2.2.13. LF uses split('
'), retaining form feeds; sourcecoverage.md gives complete boundaries. PDF pages 10 and 12 were visually checked for factors and conjugation; whole-PDF visual reading is not claimed. Publisher-identical 2001 bytes are not asserted.

DPS exp(−2φ) requires φ=u/2, so I_DPS(mφ)=I_book(mu). Also i∂∂̄φ=πdd^cu and πθ+i∂∂̄φ=π(θ+dd^cu); a source loss εω becomes εω/π. Local 1/(2m) Bergman logarithms must be doubled. Remark 2.2.2 expressly warns that the final equisingular step loses logarithmic poles. Step 3 almost decrease is for one fixed cover. The final theorem is not substituted for finite prescribed-ideal approximants in the new proof. The observations and correction are detailed in P14.8-paper.tex Sections 2, 9–10, argument.md, and source-application-ledger.md. A source range can be rerun with `python read_bound.py dps 736 775`; this verifies extraction, not the mathematics.

notes.summary: Proved all-real-index sufficiency of explicit finite ideal-norm certificates: usc upper tails are quasi-psh, decrease without collapse, and the capped integral test equals exact multiplier-ideal membership. No strong openness or positive mass is used.
notes.detailedSummary: Input is a full array A_c, c>0, of nonzero coherent ideals on connected compact Kähler X. Finite prescribed-ideal norms Φ_j at m_j=2^j have θ-loss ε_j↓0 and uniformly bounded, noncollapsed suprema. Compatibility requires a local U/C independent of j and integer cap R for the decreasing N-limit of integrals against min(R,exp(−c max_{j≤k≤N}Φ_k)). The raw supremum and its usc regularization agree a.e. by L¹ distributional positivity and canonical value recovery. Compact nested superlevel sets and decreasing psh mean-value propagation exclude collapse. DCT in N and MCT in R and j give the exact extended integral at u, realizing every real index. The proof uses precisely disclosed ordinary psh representation and mean-value premises and excludes arbitrary unknown psh corrections.
notes.text:
Fix connected compact Kähler X, a smooth closed θ representing a pseudoeffective class, Kähler ω, dd^c=(i/2π)∂∂̄, and I(cu) defined by integrability of |f|²e^(−cu). The index convention is all real c>0. Do not infer integer/full-real I-equivalence from this theorem. Let arbitrary nonzero coherent A_c be the input.

A witness consists of known finite holomorphic norm formulas Φ_j of exactly A_{m_j}, m_j=2^j. A rigid permissible presentation is a finite maximum on known nested chart balls: (1/m_j)log Σ|g_{j,a,ℓ}|²−ρ_a+(Lβ_a+A)/m_j, with finite generating tuples of A_{m_j}, known fixed geometric potentials dd^cρ_a=θ and smooth barriers, and explicit omission of boundary branches or agreeing chart transitions. The definition also permits equivalent known Hermitian ideal norms. Arbitrary unknown bounded or psh corrections are excluded. Require θ+dd^cΦ_j≥−ε_jω, ε_j↓0, and −B≤sup_XΦ_j≤B. Individual Φ_j need not decrease.

Set H_{j,N}=max_{j≤k≤N}Φ_k. For every germ f at x and every real c>0 require f∈A_{c,x} iff some coordinate ball U containing x, with closure in a domain of holomorphic representation of f, and C<∞ satisfy, for every j and integer R≥1,
lim_N ∫_U |f|²min(R,e^(−cH_{j,N}))dV≤C.
C and U may depend on c,x,f, but not j,R. The N limit decreases and is bounded; all finite-N capped integrals are finite. At a −∞ pole the cap is R. At a simultaneous zero of f the capped product is zero, and the untruncated product is defined by these caps. This avoids 0·∞.

For fixed j, H_{j,N} is (θ+ε_jω)-psh, since maxima preserve a common lower curvature bound. It increases and has the integrable lower bound Φ_j and a uniform upper bound. Dominated convergence gives L¹_loc convergence to S_j=sup_{k≥j}Φ_k. Positivity passes in distributions. Its canonical quasi-psh representative v_j majorizes each H_{j,N} pointwise: the a.e. inequality implies the pointwise one by adding a local smooth potential and taking shrinking psh averages. Thus S_j*≤v_j. Conversely those same averages, bounded by local suprema of S_j, give v_j≤S_j*. Therefore Ψ_j=S_j* is (θ+ε_jω)-psh and equals S_j a.e.

The Ψ_j decrease with suprema at least −B. The nested nonempty compact sets {Ψ_j≥−B−1} have a common point, so their pointwise limit is finite there. Add local potentials of θ+ε_1ω for a common lower curvature bound. The sub-mean inequality at a point with a common lower value bounds the negative-part integral on a ball. Fixed positive-volume overlaps then give a common lower value at some overlap point for every j; a ball there containing the next smaller chart ball propagates the integral bound. Choose a finite connected chain of small balls with compact overlaps and bounded smooth-potential differences. Monotone convergence of a common upper bound minus these decreasing psh functions gives local L¹ convergence to a nontrivial limit. The limit is usc and agrees with its canonical representative by sub-mean values and recovery by averages. Distributional positivity with ε_j→0 gives u=lim Ψ_j∈PSH(X,θ), and compactness globalizes L¹ convergence. This is the standard decreasing-sequence machinery with its premises and propagation argument explicit; no net compactness theorem or hidden mass condition is imported.

For fixed U,c,f,j,R, DCT in N with bound R|f|² gives the integral of |f|²min(R,e^(−cΨ_j)), using raw/usc a.e. equality. MCT as integer R→∞ gives the uncapped integral, possibly infinite. Since Ψ_j↓u, a second MCT in j gives the exact identity
sup_{j,R} lim_N ∫_U|f|²min(R,e^(−cH_{j,N}))dV = ∫_U|f|²e^(−cu)dV.
The local-ball quantifiers now give I(cu)_x=A_{c,x} for every c, not merely the witness degrees. This is a proof of sufficiency and explicit reconstruction from a certificate, not by itself necessity. It needs only the ordinary canonical psh-distribution/mean-value inputs named in the paper and measure theory. It does not use strong openness, the frozen bad union formula, or positive top mass. Full reasoning appears in P14.8-paper.tex Sections 3–4 and argument.md. The programs do not verify this continuum proof.

notes.summary: Author proof of exact necessity interface R using finite weighted Hilbert generators, relative finite kernel reduction, and exact-potential fixed-cover gluing. It imports named published Hörmander/OT/Nadel/Cartan inputs with explicit scopes; full original-primary validation of those imports remains unavailable.
notes.detailedSummary: For every θ-psh u the draft constructs finite global ideal norms of exactly I(mu), with curvature loss O(1/m), uniform upper/noncollapse bounds, Φ_m≥u, and usc upper tails decreasing pointwise exactly to u, including polar points. Hilbert sections generate the multiplier ideal via point-pole ∂̄ solutions, Artin–Rees and Nakayama. A coherent product ideal and Fréchet openness yield P≤K≤2P, avoiding an uncontrolled log C_m/m error. Exact local θ potentials give holomorphic transitions and O(1/m) overlap estimates on a fixed cover. Known barriers glue finite maxima at O(1/m) cost. OT lower bounds and uniformly local mean-value upper bounds prove exact tail equality. The target is used only to prove existence of finite tuples, not in witness syntax or tests. This is not an import of the final DPS equisingular theorem.
notes.text:
The author claims the following exact regularization interface. For every u∈PSH(X,θ), finite norm functions Φ_m can be chosen at integer m whose actual local generating ideals are exactly I(mu), with θ+dd^cΦ_m≥−C₀ω/m, Φ_m≥u, uniform upper and noncollapsed supremum bounds, and whose usc upper-tail envelopes along any increasing unbounded integer sequence decrease exactly to u. The fixed smooth geometric terms do not encode u. The construction uses u only to prove existence of the finite holomorphic tuples.

Published ordinary inputs, with exact scopes: (H) weighted Hörmander ∂̄ solutions on bounded pseudoconvex balls for a possibly singular psh W with i∂∂̄W≥i∂∂̄|z|² and finite weighted norm of ∂̄-closed (0,1)-data; solution norm bounded by data norm. (O) point OT extension on a ball, uniformly for x in an inner compact set and arbitrary psh weight W: F(x)=1 and ∫|F|²e^(−W)≤C e^(−W(x)) if W(x)>−∞. (N) nonzero coherence of multiplier ideals. (C) compact-open closedness of coherent ideal sections, Cartan B surjectivity of finite generator coefficient maps on Stein domains, and openness of the resulting continuous Fréchet surjection. The exact applications are below; these are not unnamed grants or finite convex facts. The packet lacks the full original texts for H/O/N/C; source-application-ledger.md marks that original-primary evidence interface explicitly. The mathematical proof is relative to these stated published ordinary theorems, not to a new assumed interface R.

Choose fixed nested balls B_a^0⊂⊂B_a^1⊂⊂B_a^2⊂⊂B_a^3 with the cores covering X, and fixed smooth potentials dd^cρ_a=θ. On a ball D put v=u+ρ, psh, and H_m={F holomorphic on D: ∫|F|²e^(−mv)<∞}. All its sections lie in I=I(mv)=I(mu), by smooth bounded-weight invariance.

To prove exact generation, fix x. Artin–Rees gives q with I_x∩m_x^(q+1)⊂m_x I_x. For a local weighted-integrable g∈I_x choose cutoff χ=1 near x, compactly supported in a local integrability domain. Solve ∂̄h=∂̄(χg) on D with W=mv+(n+q)log|z−x|²+|z|². This is psh with the required strict Hessian; the data avoid x so their weighted norm is finite. The solution is holomorphic near x. Local upper boundedness of v makes its point-pole integrability force ord_xh≥q+1; also h has the original weighted norm, because the extra factors of W are bounded above on D. Thus h_x∈I_x∩m_x^(q+1), and F=χg−h∈H_m has F_x≡g mod m_xI_x. Repeating for finite generators, Nakayama proves H_m generates I_x. Coherence turns stalk equality into neighborhood equality. A finite cover gives finite H_m sections generating I on a neighborhood of any smaller closed ball.

Now form the weighted Bergman kernel K_m=Σ|f_ℓ|², with an orthonormal basis whose first s members span the preceding finite generators on a slightly larger concentric Stein ball V. Mean values bound evaluation and its derivatives on compacts, so K_m is continuous and its holomorphic two-variable kernel series converges normally. On V×V̄ the coherent product ideal J is generated by f_a(z)f_b*(w), a,b≤s, where f_b*(w)=overline(f_b(overline(w))). Kernel tails T_N=Σ_{ℓ>N}f_ℓ(z)f_ℓ*(w) belong to J by closedness and tend to zero in its induced Fréchet topology. Cartan B gives a surjective coefficient map O(V×V̄)^(s²)→J(V×V̄); the open mapping theorem gives, for all sufficiently large N, coefficients representing T_N with all compact suprema less than δ/s. On the conjugate diagonal,
0≤K_m−P_N≤(δ/s)(Σ_{a≤s}|f_a|)²≤δΣ_{a≤s}|f_a|²≤δP_N.
Thus P_N≤K_m≤(1+δ)P_N uniformly on the desired compact, including ideal zeros. The finite tuple still generates exactly I. Take δ=1. No uniform-in-m division estimate or bounded generator count is assumed. This relative reduction is essential; a domination constant C_m of uncontrolled size would leave a gap.

For overlap estimates on fixed inner compact overlaps, choose a uniformly small ball inside both larger charts. Since θ is closed, ρ_b−ρ_a is pluriharmonic, hence Re t for a holomorphic t there. For F in the source Hilbert space, transfer χF exp(mt/2) to the destination ball by solving ∂̄ with W=m(u+ρ_b)+n log|z_b−z_b(x)|²+|z_b|². The weighted norm on the cutoff support is exactly the source norm: |F exp(mt/2)|²e^(−m(u+ρ_b))=|F|²e^(−m(u+ρ_a)). The derivatives of the cutoff, pole factor on its annulus, and coordinate Jacobians are uniformly bounded. H gives a solution h vanishing at x by the point pole. The destination holomorphic section has value F(x)exp(mt(x)/2) and norm at most a geometric multiple of the source norm, independent of m,u. Taking evaluation suprema and reversing charts yields
C^(−1)K_{m,a}e^(−mρ_a)≤K_{m,b}e^(−mρ_b)≤CK_{m,a}e^(−mρ_a).
Finite reduction changes the ratio by at most 2. Therefore q_{m,a}=(1/m)log P_{m,a}−ρ_a obey q_{m,b}≥q_{m,a}−D/m and its reverse, D=log(2C), as extended inequalities even at common zeros. No varying-cover dyadic almost decrease is assumed.

OT on inner compact balls gives K_{m,a}≥C_O^(−1)exp(m(u+ρ_a)), hence q_{m,a}≥u−log(2C_O)/m. At u=−∞ this is trivial. Mean values give q_{m,a}(x)≤sup_{|z_a(y)−z_a(x)|<r}u(y)+M_ρr+[log C′+2n log(1/r)]/m, uniformly at nearby points. Set A=log(2C_O). Choose β_a=1−|z_a|²/(r_a^1)² with β_a≥3/4 on cores and zero on patch boundaries, and L=4(D+1). Near a boundary a, a core b has sufficient barrier advantage to dominate that branch on a neighborhood. The extended kernel inequalities give domination also across common ideal zeros, without subtracting infinities.

Define Φ_m as the finite maximum of q_{m,a}+(Lβ_a+A)/m over active patches. Boundary omission proves global gluing. All tuples generate exactly I(mu), and two-way holomorphic generator comparisons show the maximum has that same ideal-norm type with its explicit bounded local correction. Each q branch has θ+dd^cq≥0. Known barriers have uniformly bounded negative Hessians, so finite maxima give θ+dd^cΦ_m≥−LC_βω/m. The positive shift ensures Φ_m≥u. A fixed small radius in the upper estimate gives a uniform upper bound; the lower supremum bound follows from Φ_m≥u.

For x fixed, all nearby y obey a uniform bound Φ_m(y)≤sup_{B(x,C₁r)}u+C₂r+[C₃+2n log(1/r)+A+L]/m. Pass to an upper tail and its usc regularization, let the starting m_j→∞, and then r→0. The upper bound tends to u(x) by usc, including u(x)=−∞, where every finite upper threshold holds on a sufficiently small ball. The lower tail bound is u because all Φ_m≥u. Thus the tails decrease exactly to u pointwise, not only a.e. or in L¹. Their quasi-psh status follows from the envelope argument proved in n2. This proves R and gives m_j=2^j, ε_j=(LC_β+1)/m_j certificates for every actual realization. The exact integral identity in n2 establishes the test for those certificates.

Full proof and formula syntax are in P14.8-paper.tex Section 5 and argument.md. The two key review interfaces are the coherent-product Fréchet reduction and the exact-potential L² overlap transfer. The continuum proof is not certified by the example program, successful TeX compilation, or DPS file hashes. Original source closure for all deep imports is expressly not asserted.

notes.summary: Explicit P¹ finite-norm certificates and incompatible full-real arrays, plus an independent Cantor/Jensen proof that one I-array carries every raw mass in [0,1]. Bounded exact checks made 847 assertions; they do not establish continuum analytic theorems.
notes.detailedSummary: For u=aG, 0≤a≤1, A_c=O(−floor(ac)D). Binomial holomorphic tuples at q_m=floor(am) give exactly Φ_m=(q_m/m)G and the prescribed ideals; dyadic coefficients increase to a. Unit ideals and the a=1 zero-top-mass example follow. Three coherent arrays fail monotonicity, subadditivity, or strong openness; the ceiling-minus-one array satisfies the first two constraints but misses the integer endpoint. A very thin endpoint Cantor set supports a nonatomic measure; its Green potential is −∞ exactly on the set, all scaled exponential weights are locally integrable by a small-mass Jensen estimate, and degree-one truncations yield raw mass 1−s. Thus raw representative/mass recovery remains impossible. Distinct P-envelopes require a separate theorem, not silently granted here.
notes.text:
On P¹ let ω=dd^c log(1+|z|²), D={0}, and G=log|z|²−log(1+|z|²). Then ω+dd^cG=δ₀, sup G=0. For 0≤a≤1, u=aG is ω-psh. A germ of order k at 0 has integrability condition k>ac−1, hence I(cu)=O(−floor(ac)D) for every real c>0, including integer ac.

Put q_m=floor(am). The finite tuple sqrt(binomial(m−q_m,ℓ)) z^(q_m+ℓ), 0≤ℓ≤m−q_m, generates exactly (z^q_m). Its squared norm sums to |z|^(2q_m)(1+|z|²)^(m−q_m), so (1/m)log of the sum minus log(1+|z|²) is Φ_m=(q_m/m)G. In the infinity chart take sqrt(binomial(m−q_m,ℓ))w^ℓ, which includes 1 and gives the same function. For dyadic m, q_m/m increases to a, so Φ_j decreases exactly to aG, with zero loss and suprema zero. The integral identity in n2 gives all-index compatibility. At a=0 the binomial norm gives the smooth unit array; at a=1 the finite functions are all G, whose ordinary current is δ₀ and whose degree-one nonpluripolar product is zero. On background θ=0, u=0 also gives a unit-array zero-mass example. No probability normalization is formed.

Three incompatible nonzero coherent full-real arrays on P¹ are (i) O(−D) for c<1 and O for c≥1, violating A_d⊂A_c when d>c; (ii) units for c<1 and O(−D) for c≥1, violating A₂⊂A₁² at 0; (iii) O(−(ceil c−1)D), satisfying monotonicity and subadditivity by ceil(c+d)−1≥ceil c+ceil d−2, but with 1∈A₁ and 1 outside every A_{1+δ}. Index monotonicity follows directly by normalizing the local weight above by zero. Example (ii) uses the declared DEL subadditivity theorem; example (iii) uses the declared Guan–Zhou strong openness theorem. Both inputs are local psh theorems applied after a smooth locally bounded correction for quasi-psh weights. They are not needed for the main criterion. By n2 none of these arrays can have a certificate.

Independently of any frozen capacity formula, build endpoint Cantor intervals with lengths ℓ₀=1 and ℓ_k=exp(−4^k) for k≥1. The Bernoulli probability μ gives each level-k interval mass 2^(−k), so it has no atoms and the intersection F has area zero. For x∈F, its containing level-k interval has μ-mass 2^(−k) within distance ℓ_k. Layer-cake integration yields ∫−log|x−p|dμ(p)≥Σ_{k≥1}(4^k−4^(k−1))2^(−k)=∞.

Let G_p be the squared chordal Green kernel and V=∫G_p dμ. Negative area integrals of G_p are uniformly finite by FS rotation invariance, so Fubini gives V∈L¹ and ω+dd^cV=μ. Reverse Fatou for nonpositive kernels and the integrated sub-mean inequality identify the integral with its canonical usc representative. It is finite/smooth off F and −∞ on F. In particular F is polar by this explicit potential, not by an imported capacity theorem.

For u_s=sV, 0≤s≤1, the current is (1−s)ω+sμ. Fix c>0 and x. For cs>0 choose a small disk whose doubled disk has μ-mass β<1/(cs), using nonatomicity. The far contribution to the local logarithmic potential is bounded below. Jensen for the normalized near measure gives exp(−cs∫log|z−p|²dμ_near)≤β^(−1)∫|z−p|^(−2csβ)dμ_near. This has finite area integral uniformly in p because csβ<1. The case β=0 has no near contribution. Smooth chordal corrections are bounded. Hence 1 and every bounded local holomorphic germ are integrable: I(cu_s)=O for every real c>0. For s>0 the finite locus is X minus F, where the current equals (1−s)ω; the degree-one truncation definition then gives nonpluripolar product (1−s)ω and raw mass 1−s. At s=0 the mass is one. One full real I-array therefore contains every raw mass in [0,1], excluding raw representative or raw mass recovery from it. This also persists after subtracting suprema. A further P-envelope distinction would require the separate P-envelope mass-preservation theorem and is not granted by this calculation.

The exact finite example-input.json grid was checked by the fresh author program verify_examples.py. It made 847 successful assertions on radial floor thresholds, binomial identities at rational points, dyadic coefficient inequalities, the bad smaller-exponent union, ceiling constraints, and Cantor summands. The finite loops are exhaustive only for that saved grid. The continuum results are the proofs just given, not extrapolations from program success. Rerun `python verify_examples.py`; detailed rows are in example-output.json. P14.8-paper.tex Sections 7–8 and argument.md contain the full calculations.

notes.detailedSummary: Combining n2 and n3 yields iff existence for arbitrary all-real coherent arrays, with no unknown target in the admissibility tests and no arbitrary psh correction. The chosen witness constructs a θ-psh realization of all indices; necessity is proved from a realization rather than assumed as R. n4 preserves the raw-I/mass obstruction, and n1 quarantines the false source formula. notes.text:
The exact claimed mathematical solution is this: for connected compact Kähler X, smooth closed pseudoeffective θ and Kähler ω, an arbitrary full real array of nonzero coherent ideals A_c is realizable as I(cu), c>0, by some nontrivial θ-psh u if and only if there exists a finite prescribed-ideal norm certificate with vanishing curvature loss, bounded/noncollapsed suprema, and the uniform capped integral compatibility condition stated in n2. No positive mass is required. The witnesses have finite holomorphic tuples and fixed known geometric smooth terms with explicit finite gluing, not unknown target potentials or arbitrary psh/bounded corrections.

Proof: n2 constructs the decreasing usc upper-tail limit of any such certificate, proves it is nontrivial θ-psh and that the capped test is exactly integrability of |f|²e^(−cu), including infinite values and every real index. Thus every certified arbitrary array is realized and an unrealizable array cannot pass the test. Conversely, given any θ-psh realization, n3 proves exact R: weighted sections generate exactly its I(mu), a finite relative reduction retains their kernel bounds, exact local θ-potentials yield fixed-cover O(1/m) gluing and curvature loss, and uniform small-ball upper estimates plus the lower bound give tail envelopes decreasing exactly to the original u, even at poles. The integral identity from n2 then proves that realization's certificates pass the all-index test. R is proved, not imported from working305 or the DPS final theorem. This establishes necessity as well as sufficiency.

This is a noncircular witness characterization in the explicit infinite functional-analytic sense allowed by the assignment. Its input is the bare formal ideal array and geometry; its tests quantify over finite holomorphic norm expressions and scalar/curvature/integral inequalities, without an unknown psh target. The target occurs only in the proof that witnesses exist for a realizable array. No effective finite algebraic axiom system or decision procedure is claimed. An independent reviewer must assess the proof and whether this witness characterization satisfies the intended originality/scope of the formal-data alternative; it is not automatically an accepted paper or an inventory closure. If a stronger interpretation requires effective ideal-only algebraic admissibility, that stronger problem is not solved here.

The theorem uses the precisely scoped ordinary published H/OT/Nadel/Cartan inputs listed in n3 and source-application-ledger.md, together with ordinary psh mean values and local algebra. The packet does not contain their complete original primaries; full original-primary source closure for those imports is therefore explicitly unvalidated. This is the exact remaining source-evidence gate, not a hidden unproved R hypothesis. A full review should especially inspect the coherent-product Fréchet topology/open-mapping reduction and exact-potential L² transfer. Execution success cannot establish their correctness. The separate subadditivity and strong-openness imports affect n4's obstruction examples and n1's corrected formula, not the main theorem.

The output raw u can depend on witness norms. Normalizing u−sup_Xu does not yield certificate independence. A canonical normalized I-model would require a separately validated I-envelope theorem. n4 independently proves the raw mass/representative obstruction: one unit I-array has raw masses [0,1]. No P-type recovery, all-semivaluation formula, new zero-mass DXZ interval, or probability normalization at zero mass is asserted.
